jobs.title: Commercial Strategy Manager
jobs.description: Overview About the role: This is a high‑impact strategy role at the heart of PepsiCo UKI’s Commercial function. As Commercial Strategy Manager, you will be the strategic right-hand to our Commercial Vice President and Sales Leadership Team, shaping the long-term commercial strategy, solving the hardest problems, and building the narratives that influence how PepsiCo shows up with its biggest customers. This role is ideal for an experienced strategy consultant looking to move into industry while retaining the problem quality, senior exposure, and pace of a consulting environment, with the added benefit of end‑to‑end ownership and delivery. Responsibilities What you’ll do: Shape the commercial strategy Partner with the Commercial VP and Sales Leadership Team as a trusted advisor on the most complex and ambiguous commercial questions. Lead the long-term and short-term commercial planning processes — growth outlook, sub-channel strategy, annual operating plan. Own the strategic outputs that define PepsiCo's commercial narrative: category strategy, customer narratives, and the growth story. Drive strategic initiatives from concept to impact Lead priority commercial initiatives end-to-end, from diagnosis and business case through to delivery and measurement. Own the governance, portfolio management, and integrated roadmap: milestones, risks, resources, and investment. Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure tangible commercial outcomes, not just strategic recommendations. Be the strategic go-to for Commercial Leadership Build the strategic storyline for internal and external forums. Act as a chief of staff to the VP of Sales, handling high-priority, time-sensitive requests with precision and judgement. Maintain a sharp external lens: consumer trends, competitive moves, macroeconomic and geopolitical shifts that shape the commercial agenda. Qualifications What you’ll bring: Consulting-grade problem structuring – you frame problems clearly, test hypotheses rigorously, and land on a "so what" that drives action. Comfort in ambiguity with senior stakeholders – you can walk into a room of Directors and VPs with a half-formed problem and leave with a clear path forward. Storytelling that drives decisions – you translate analysis into compelling, executive-ready narratives that shift the conversation. Bias to delivery – you don't just recommend; you own outcomes. You hold yourself accountable for commercial impact, not just strategic output. Intellectual curiosity – you stay on top of what's happening outside PepsiCo as much as inside it. You bring fresh thinking from other industries, markets, and categories. Requirements: 5+ years' experience, ideally including 3+ years at a top-tier strategy consulting firm or an FMCG in-house strategy / commercial excellence team. Strong commercial and strategic judgement. Proven ability to influence and operate credibly with senior leaders (Director / VP level and above). Outstanding analytical skills and structured problem-solving. Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive presentations for C-suite audiences. Ability to lead complex, cross-functional agendas autonomously in a matrixed organisation.

jobs.title: A&M Excellence Marketing Transformation Director
jobs.description: Overview This position is responsible for the overarching Global A&M Excellence agenda, as part of the broader S&T and Global Marketing transformation. The person will define key talent and resource requirements for the on-going projects of the A&M Excellence agenda, defining annual scope of work for the capability while aligning market and regional level senior stakeholders through contracting, design and delivery of individual projects. The role will require the individual to work with the Global SVP level stakeholders across Media, Content, Transformation, Insights, D&AI as well as local and regional level CMOs, Media leads, Marketers and S&T delivery teams to drive transformation of Global A&M in line with the agenda objectives and established KPIs. Responsibilities Own overall delivery of the Global A&M Excellence Service as part of the broader S&T consumer transformation. Partner with Global / Regional / BU Functional leads to ensure the project is aligned and consistent with other Global / Regional / BU transformation aims. Develop executive level materials for Global / Regional / BU SVP level leaders throughout the year to drive awareness of the capability, its plans and its results. Clearly articulate the Service’s vision, outcomes, KPIs, accomplishments and opportunities as required. Manage all internal and external relationships in support of the creation and execution of the plan. Create and execute the stakeholder alignment programme to deliver both customer understanding of the rationale for change and the value of change. Work with Global/Regional/Local Marketing and S&T business partners to define service scope that supports the ever evolving needs of all three major regions: North America, International Foods and International Beverages. Manage a diverse team of 9+ individuals based across multiple time-zones, countries and cultural backgrounds (team is located in Krakow (KCC) and India (ICC)). Ensuring strong people management practices in place to foster a supportive and productive team engagement that recognizes and accelerates top talent and builds positive Org health scores annually. Continuously evaluate and update talent strategy, structure and organizational design in line with evolving business needs. Align and engage with Snr Director, SVPs and HRBPs to execute people plans. Coach and mentor L11 and L10 direct reports to build future pipeline of people managers. Implement continuous improvement approach by codifying new learnings from A&M analysis, A&M Allocation while integrating new, emerging measurement frameworks to modernize annual deliverables from the capability to the business. Maintain an external mindset, including staying on top of consumer, competitive, AI for Marketing and macroeconomic / geopolitical trends shaping marketing organisation and our business. Working in close partnership with A&M Data & Governance Director, own the overall A&M reporting cadence to BU/Regional/Global Leadership on a quarterly/annual/ and ad-hoc basis, as needed. Provide and continuously update Global guidance on A&M Guidelines by brand role, Shape of A&M, and maintain one source of truth for Competitive benchmarking. Support Global S&T and Global Marketing to track key A&M performance indicators by providing automated solutions (e.g. A&M Hub) to enhance speed and accessibility to data. Provide an annual A&M AOP Contracting Service to International Foods. Qualifications 10+ years Marketing experience, including 3+ years in marketing leadership position Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, along with the ability to influence and demonstrate confidence in communications with senior level management Proven record of Marketing Transformation is a must Knowledge of key PEP marketing partners /agencies Strong leadership, organizational and interpersonal skills. Comfortable managing trade-offs and resolving conflict. Experience managing a culturally diverse senior stakeholder group. Strong project management skills; track record of overseeing a complex task resolution, gained in PepsiCo, a similar corporate or as an external consultant Excellent analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills Experience working with AI and automation tools for PPT and Excel like PowerBI, ThinkCell and Co-Pilot Pro. Leadership within a matrix organization, incl demonstrated experience of operating at Exec level Ability to lead process transformation with strong change management skill set Flexibility in adjusting & reprioritizing to meet changing needs in a fast-paced environment Self-motivated/self-starter with the ability to work independently Compensation and Benefits: The expected starting compensation range for this position is 383,000 PLN annually (gross). Location, confirmed job-related skills, experience, and education will be considered in setting actual starting salary. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range during the hiring process. This role is eligible for an annual bonus of 25% and premium bonus of 10% of annual salary, based on performance and eligibility. In addition to salary, PepsiCo offers a comprehensive benefits package to support our employees and their families, subject to elections and eligibility.

jobs.title: Senior Strategy Manager - Away From Home
jobs.description: Overview PepsiCo is a playground for curious people. We invite thinkers, doers, and changemakers to champion innovation, take calculated risks, and challenge the status quo. From executives to team members on the front lines, we’re excited about the future. We take chances. Together, we dare to make the world a better place. Our associates are the magic ingredient. Each of them plays an integral role in helping create deep connections between people and our products. Think about your last group celebration: chances are, one of our iconic brands was by your side. At PepsiCo, you’re invited to be a part of a global team of innovators who make, move, and sell these products—which are enjoyed by more than 1 billion people a day. A career at PepsiCo means working in a culture where everyone’s welcome. Here, you can dare to be yourself. No matter who you are or where you’re from, you can influence the people around you and the world at large. By showing up, you’ll have the opportunity to learn, develop and grow your skills for the future. Our supportive teams can fuel your professional goals to make a global impact on people and the planet.Join us. Dare for Better PepsiCo Away From Home (“AFH”) is a division of PepsiCo that brings the company's entire portfolio of food and beverage brands to market in out-of-home consumption channels. The AFH operating environment is complex and highly dynamic, requiring diverse sales and go-to-market systems to meet consumer needs at work, at play, and on the go. PepsiCo AFH leverages the scale and breadth of the company's brands to provide a unified voice to its customers and deliver a competitive advantage in the fast-growing AFH channel. Responsibilities What’s Your Role? As a Sr. Strategy Manager on the AFH Strategy team is part of PepsiCo’s broader Strategy network and works globally across PepsiCo’s entire portfolio of beverages, snacks and nutrition. Our function plays a critical role in charting PepsiCo’s long-term growth and portfolio development, driving both the future of the company and shaping the industry landscape. AFH is a key enabler of PepsiCo’s strategy, serving as a source of profitable growth, a vehicle to build our brands, and a transformation accelerator. We are tasked with ensuring the company invests in the assets and capabilities needed to stay ahead of the competition, adapt to market trends, and maintain market leadership. This entails developing actionable solutions for some of the most challenging issues facing the company by influencing brand, innovation, equipment and channel priorities and by undertaking transformational initiatives (e.g., data & analytics, online ordering) to achieve the greatest possible growth and penetration. Our team primarily works across three types of projects: long term strategic planning, annual strategic planning, and growth priorities (e.g., channel / customer strategy, portfolio, etc.). What Will Make You Succeed: Employ solution-oriented mindset to help solve an array of PepsiCo’s most challenging, business critical, topics Translate business problems to structured projects that you will lead in end-to-end delivery against key objectives, from hypothesis development to final materials Lead analytical workstreams – identify and deconstruct business issues, and develop strategic, analytical, and financial frameworks to conduct analyses and solve critical business issues with minimal oversight from functional leaders Demonstrate strong leadership and influence management skills, including the ability to challenge the status quo Lead & manage teams to deliver on-time and complete deliverables Invest in the professional development of direct reports including coaching, performance reviews, and long-term career guidance Build executive-ready project deliverables Execute against time-sensitive requests from Executive leaders and cross-functional business partners Maintain an external mindset, including staying on top of consumer, competitive, and macroeconomic / geopolitical trends Contribute to capability building for the entire Global Strategy function (e.g., Recruiting, Training, Knowledge Management) Compensation and Benefits: The expected compensation range for this position is between $123,500 - $206,750. Location, confirmed job-related skills, experience, and education will be considered in setting actual starting salary. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range during the hiring process. Bonus based on performance and eligibility target payout is 15% of annual salary paid out annually. Paid time off subject to eligibility, including paid parental leave, vacation, sick, and bereavement. In addition to salary, PepsiCo offers a comprehensive benefits package to support our employees and their families, subject to elections and eligibility: Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Health, and Dependent Care Reimbursement Accounts, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Insurance (Accident, Group Legal, Life), Defined Contribution Retirement Plan. Qualifications Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s Degree required 5 years of strategy experience either internally or with a Top Tier consulting firm Plus to have: MBA preferred 7 years of strategy experience either internally or with a Top Tier consulting firm preferred Expertise in competitive analysis, market trends, and food and beverage consumer behavior preferred. Experience in management consulting for CPG clients preferred. Passionate about the Consumer-Packaged Goods ("CPG") industry and love for our brands. Skills and Competencies: Strategic mindset with an ability to think broadly, refine questions, and develop analytical frameworks. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and translate it into actionable business strategies. Excellent technical skills to coach teams to analyze large quantities of data error-free. Outstanding project and people management experience with the ability to drive initiatives from concept to execution and a proven record of managing teams or projects cross-functionally. Demonstrated high emotional intelligence and strong ability to "manage up". Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to educate, engage, and influence senior executives and stakeholders. Global outlook with sensitivity and awareness of social and cultural differences. Proven ability to work collaboratively across different functions and regions. This position is limited to persons with indefinite right to work in the United States. Role is open to professionals who can work from Purchase, NY. EEO Statement Our Company will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, and all other applicable laws, including but not limited to, San Francisco Police Code Sections 4901-4919, commonly referred to as the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance; and Chapter XVII, Article 9 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code, commonly referred to as the Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability status. PepsiCo is an Equal Opportunity Employer: Female / Minority / Disability / Protected Veteran / Sexual Orientation / Gender Identity / Age. If you'd like more information about your EEO rights as an applicant under the law, please download the available EEO is the Law & EEO is the Law Supplement documents. View PepsiCo EEO Policy. Please view our Pay Transparency Statement

jobs.title: Corporate Strategy Manager - Korea
jobs.description: Overview Work for a global FMCG company with some of the world’s most trusted and iconic brands. Be part of an exciting business where employees are recognized and career growth is supported.  At PepsiCo, you can Dare for Better. You can help build a world where there are more possibilities for more people, no matter what role you hold. Together, we’ll make a positive impact for good. Because when we Dare for Better, we can smile at what’s next. For our careers, families, communities and the planet. The Corporate Strategy Manager - Korea accelerates growth across the North Asia beverage system by combining strategic insight, commercial analytics, and transformation leadership. This role serves as a strategic thought partner to the GM and a key interface with bottler partners, helping shape business priorities, resolve complex commercial issues, and drive sustainable value creation across the PepsiCo–bottler system. The role requires a strong balance of strategic thinking, analytical rigor, commercial acumen, stakeholder influence, and the ability to translate strategy into execution. Responsibilities What you will be responsible for: 1.Generate Strategic Insights Leverage commercial, market, consumer, and competitive insights to identify high-impact growth opportunities across categories, brands, channels, customers, and portfolio mix. Translate complex data and analytics into clear, actionable strategic recommendations for the holistic business strategy set up and execution. Develop fact-based perspectives on key business opportunities, risks, and strategic choices. 2. Data & Business Intelligence Own and connect key data sources, including internal shipment sales data, external POS, market share, consumer, and category analytics. Establish a fact base to support strategic decision-making and performance management. Continuously identify new data sources, consumer research data and analytical approaches to improve business understanding and decision quality. 3. Act as a Strategic Thought Partner to the GM & Bottler Leadership Partner closely with the GM and bottler commercial/RGM leadership to diagnose business challenges, shape strategic priorities, and influence decision-making through structured, data-driven insights. Bring an objective PepsiCo perspective while understanding and balancing bottler economics and business priorities. Challenge assumptions constructively and develop practical, mutually beneficial solutions to complex business issues. 4. Lead Franchise Governance & Bottler Negotiations Partner closely with the GM to lead the Franchise Governance agenda with bottler partners, ensuring alignment on strategic priorities, business performance, commercial plans, and critical franchise matters. Build trusted relationships with bottler leadership and proactively manage communication, alignment, and negotiation on key franchise agendas. Prepare and lead governance forums, including agenda setting, issue framing, decision making, and follow-up, in close partnership with the GM. Drive resolution of complex or potentially contentious issues by developing fact-based positions, understanding both PepsiCo and bottler economics, and negotiating sustainable outcomes. Identify potential areas of misalignment early and work with the GM and cross-functional teams to proactively address risks and unlock opportunities. Lead and/or coordinate key franchise agreements and governance matters, including Exclusive Bottling Agreement (EBA), Non-Compete Clause Compliance, Business Development Agreement (BDA), Concentrate Supply Agreement (CSA), Concentrate Price Change and other franchise-governance related matters. Ensure strong governance discipline, clear accountability, and timely follow-through on agreed actions and decisions. 5. Innovation Commercialization Build robust business cases and approval memos for new product launches and major commercial initiatives. Develop concentrate pricing recommendations based on PepsiCo and bottler economics (P&L Assumptions). Lead commercial discussions and negotiations with bottler partners to secure alignment, appropriate value sharing, and sustainable profitability. Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure strategic innovations are translated into commercially viable and executable plans. 6. Lead Cross-Functional Strategic Initiatives Scope and lead high-impact strategic projects across PepsiCo and bottler teams. Mobilize cross-functional expertise across Marketing, Sales, Finance, R&D, Supply Chain, Legal, and other functions to solve complex business challenges. Drive projects from problem definition through recommendation, alignment, execution, and measurable business impact. Lead transformation initiatives that strengthen commercial capabilities and the overall PepsiCo–bottler system. 7. Performance Management & Execution Establish strong operating rhythms, performance tracking, and governance mechanisms to ensure disciplined execution against strategic priorities. Monitor key business and commercial KPIs, identify performance gaps, and translate findings into actionable interventions. Enable rapid problem solving and cross-functional alignment to sustain delivery of business results. 8. Stakeholder Management Build trusted relationships and influence stakeholders across PepsiCo and bottler organizations, from working-level teams to senior leadership. Effectively navigate complex organizational dynamics and different stakeholder interests. Communicate complex strategic and commercial topics with clarity, conviction, and executive presence. Serve as a bridge between PepsiCo functions and bottler teams to accelerate alignment and execution. 9. Ad-hoc Business Analysis & Strategic Problem Solving Own ad-hoc commercial, consumer, financial, and data analyses to support critical business decisions. Quickly structure ambiguous business questions, develop hypotheses, analyze available data, and translate findings into clear recommendations. Provide timely analytical and strategic support on emerging business issues and opportunities. 10. GM & Strategic Initiative Support Provide flexible, high-priority support to the GM across evolving business needs and strategic initiatives. Support the GM on critical innovation, commercial, franchise, organizational, and cross-functional priorities. Prepare executive-level materials, recommendations, and decision frameworks for senior leadership discussions and governance forums. Act as a trusted extension of the GM in driving follow-up, alignment, and execution on priority initiatives. Qualifications What you will need to have: +10 to 15years of experience in a multinational FMCG environment within Commercial or Strategy functions, NRM or RGM functions, Insight Functions for analytical or Consulting experience with exposure to FMCG. Bachelor’s degree in any relevant field from a reputable academic institution Strong quantitative and qualitative analytical capability with structured problem-solving skills and the ability to translate data into actionable business insights Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including clear strategic storytelling and high-quality executive presentations Humble, growth-oriented mindset with strong ownership and a win-win solutions-driven attitude Collaborative working style with the ability to influence and align senior stakeholders Fluent in English, Korean language proficiency preferred. Additional Japanese language proficiency will be an advantage

jobs.title: Business Strategy Sr Manager
jobs.description: Overview At PepsiCo, we’re more than just iconic brands — we’re a team of 2,000+ passionate people across 11 countries, working together to deliver great-tasting products that consumers enjoy every day. With over 70 years in the region, we operate from 7 key locations — including 4 headquarters and 4 production sites — and offer a portfolio of 16 brands, from global icons like Pepsi and Lay’s to local favorites like Duyvis and Schwip Schwap. We’re committed to sustainability, innovation, and community impact. If you’re looking to grow your career with purpose, we’d love to hear from you. The Strategy Snr manager will work in the EMEA strategy team on key end-to-end strategy projects aligned to the EMEA growth strategy. This role will be leading analysis, problem solving, deliverables preparation for PepsiCo Executives, leveraging internal and external insights. This role will also be supporting adhoc EMEA CEO Chief of Staff deliverables and building the EMEA Strategy Capability & Community. Responsibilities This role will support a broad range of ever changing set of cross-functional strategic projects as determined by the organisational priorities taking a lead role in running the project team. The topics for these projects can be highly varied from addressing broad-based strategic questions, M&A or tactical executional obstacles. This role will lead projects autonomously: Identify and deconstruct business issues and develop strategic, analytical, and financial frameworks to conduct analyses Build "Executive ready" project deliverables Demonstrate strong leadership and significant influence management skills with the ability to gain credibility with Sr Leadership while challenging the status quo Build robust financial/strategic models (requiring strong strategical modelling and xls capability) Maintain an external mindset, including staying on top of consumer, channel, competitive, and macroeconomic / geopolitical trends Communicate the implications of the analysis to EMEA Strategy executives clearly via impactful, concise, presentation materials with compelling storytelling for executive audience Collaborate effectively, with external and/or internal stakeholders across the organisation. Develop implementation plans to drive execution with sound and highly efficient planning and project oversight Additionally, this role will support ad-hoc projects across full breadth of team including Chief of Staff deliverables as required. This will include responsibilities such as preparing board papers on key topics and other key decision making support to both the EMEA CEO, his extended leadership team and the broader global organisation. Finally, this role will contribute to build the Strategic Capability and Strategy community in EMEA by sharing best practices and partenering close with Global, Region and OU Strategy teams whenever possible. Qualifications Differentiating Competencies Consumer packaged goods or retail experience, especially food and beverages sector 10+ years of relevant experience in a variety of positions both internally and externally BA required (MBA strongly preferred) Thinks strategically and is able to codify the long term growth plan for the organization Operates efficiently and effectively in a matrixed environment and demonstrates effective collaboration across multiple layers Shows a strong ability to influence senior leaders or cross-functional teams Global outlook with sensitivity and awareness of social and cultural differences Actively participates in both global and regional strategic initiatives Key Skills and Experience Required Bright, self-starting, innovative thinker who is passionate about consumer products Structured logical thinker with ability to define problems and frameworks, demonstrate an understanding of key value drivers Able to collaborate within teams Able to complete complex analytical tasks with limited supervision Intellectual curiosity – awareness of emerging trends and competitive activity in the sustainability space Cultural sensitivity – Understand cultural and social differences in key markets and potential secondary markets with passion for understanding global differences Comfort in ambiguity – Adaptability in less-structured environments (able to “jump in” and contribute even when facts are not yet 100% clear); ability to quickly figure out solutions to complex issues Is persistent and resilient in the pursuit of objectives, can shift gears easily, is willing to take on new challenges and works to resolve issues Can effectively communicate (verbal and written) with internal and external stakeholders across all levels High attention to detail and focus on driving processes through successful execution

jobs.title: 2027 Full Time: Strategic Finance Associate Manager- MBA
jobs.description: Overview SMILE AT WHAT’S NEXT At PepsiCo, you'll find the opportunity to grow your career, make an impact, and help shape what's next. As one of the world's leading food and beverage companies, our beloved brands—including Gatorade, Lay's, and Quaker—help create smiles with every sip and bite. Behind our products is a connected system that starts with how we source and grow ingredients alongside farmers and extends to how we make, move, and deliver products while driving positive impact for our business and communities. At the heart of PepsiCo are our people: professionals who bring curiosity, drive, and fresh thinking, working together to turn ideas into action. Across functions, teams, and markets, we collaborate to solve challenges, unlock new opportunities, and create meaningful impact for our consumers, customers, and communities. No matter your role, you'll be part of a connected community where your contributions matter, your voice is heard, and your development is supported. With opportunities to grow, belong, and smile, PepsiCo offers more than a place to build your career—it offers the chance to help create what's next. Mandatory Requirement: Please upload a cover letter and resume as one document via the Resume Upload section of the application. Responsibilities Functional Description: Put your financial experience to work for some of the world’s most beloved brands with a career at PepsiCo. With many billion-dollar brands sold in over 200 countries and territories around the globe, you’ll have opportunities to help shape the future of one of the world’s largest companies. PepsiCo Finance partners have a seat at the table across all facets and functions within the company. As a Finance professional, you’ll have the opportunity to explore a multi-disciplinary career path across a broad number of functions, and contribute meaningfully towards creating smiles for consumers, driving full-potential performance and achieving our Winning with Purpose vision. All finance roles are grounded in the following capability areas: Data‑Anchored Problem Solving – Using data, metrics, and structured analysis to define problems, assess trade‑offs, and enable informed decision‑making. Finance Culture & Capability Building – Fostering financial acumen, continuous learning, and strong ways of working while actively developing individual and team capabilities. Finance Through Digitalization – Applying technology, digital tools, and process improvements to deliver efficient, accurate, and scalable outcomes. Strategic Business Partnering – Partnering with stakeholders to understand business priorities, balance competing demands, and deliver insights that drive value. PepsiCo Finance is made up of the following functional areas across all divisions, unless otherwise noted: Brand and Marketing Finance builds annual and long-term strategic brand plans, prepares the business case for new innovation, and manages marketing budgets across all brands. Associates partner with Marketing and other cross-functional teams to build plans, allocate resources, and performance manage against KPIs. Financial Planning manages sector and corporate financial performance through action-oriented analytical insights and traditional financial tools. FP&A associates focus on the development of monthly forecasts, the annual operating plan, and the three-year strategic plan. FP&A partners with senior management to prepare presentations for the Executive Committee and Wall Street. Sales / Commercial Finance works with Customer Teams to drive sustainable revenue and profit growth with our customers. Sales Finance Associates build the revenue plan, working with Sales to optimize promotional spending and manage trade spend liabilities. They proactively manage portfolio mix to drive margin improvement. Revenue Management sets retail pricing and package architecture strategy, advises on customer portfolio strategy and optimizes trade spend. Revenue Management Associates assess consumer and category trends, the customer landscape, and the competitive environment to develop these recommendations. Supply Chain Finance manages the company’s product manufacturing and distribution strategies by analyzing production, labor, transportation, and selling costs. Supply Chain associates assess the historical and projected financial economics of producing and selling company products. Associates also evaluate productivity initiatives and perform capacity analyses to drive critical capital decisions and inform production planning. Mergers & Acquisitions is responsible for executing a wide range of transactions, including acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, and strategic alliances. M&A associates get involved from the outset of a potential transaction and work closely with Corporate Finance and business units throughout the process. Associates focus on structuring the transaction, leading due diligence, developing financial models, assisting with the business case, and managing the internal approval process. Treasury manages corporate liquidity as well as foreign exchange and commodity exposure. jobs.title: 2027 Full Time: Strategic Finance Associate Analyst
jobs.description: Overview SMILE AT WHAT’S NEXT At PepsiCo, you'll find the opportunity to grow your career, make an impact, and help shape what's next. As one of the world's leading food and beverage companies, our beloved brands—including Gatorade, Lay's, and Quaker—help create smiles with every sip and bite. Behind our products is a connected system that starts with how we source and grow ingredients alongside farmers and extends to how we make, move, and deliver products while driving positive impact for our business and communities. At the heart of PepsiCo are our people: professionals who bring curiosity, drive, and fresh thinking, working together to turn ideas into action. Across functions, teams, and markets, we collaborate to solve challenges, unlock new opportunities, and create meaningful impact for our consumers, customers, and communities. No matter your role, you'll be part of a connected community where your contributions matter, your voice is heard, and your development is supported. With opportunities to grow, belong, and smile, PepsiCo offers more than a place to build your career—it offers the chance to help create what's next. Responsibilities Finance Analysts at PepsiCo are challenged to think both strategically and analytically to solve critical business problems. PepsiCo Finance partners have a seat at the table and a strong voice in the conversation across the company. Finance professionals rotate through different teams over the course of their careers in order to develop well-rounded technical and functional skills. All roles are highly cross-functional and require strong influencing skills. All finance roles are grounded in the following capability areas: Data‑Anchored Problem Solving – Using data, metrics, and structured analysis to define problems, assess trade‑offs, and enable informed decision-making. Finance Culture & Capability Building – Fostering financial acumen, continuous learning, and strong ways of working while actively developing individual and team capabilities. Finance Through Digitalization – Applying technology, digital tools, and process improvements to deliver efficient, accurate, and scalable outcomes. Strategic Business Partnering – Partnering with stakeholders to understand business priorities, balance competing demands, and deliver insights that drive value. PepsiCo Finance is made up of the following functional areas across all divisions: Brand and Innovation Finance builds annual and long-term strategic brand plans, prepares the business case for innovation and manages marketing budgets across all brands. Associates partner with Marketing and other cross-functional teams to build plans, allocate resources and performance manage against KPIs. Financial Planning manages sector and corporate financial performance through action-oriented analytical insights and traditional financial tools. FP&A associates focus on the development of monthly forecasts, the annual operating plan, and the three-year strategic plan. FP&A partners with senior management to prepare presentations for the Executive Committee and Wall Street. National Account/Customer Finance partners with the Sales organization to develop key customer strategies and manage performance. Associates develop customers’ annual operating plans, quarterly business plans, and period forecasts, analyze promotional activity and recommend trade spend allocation. Revenue Management sets pricing and package architecture strategy and advises customer portfolio strategy. Revenue Management Associates assess consumer and category trends, the customer landscape and the competitive environment to develop these recommendations. Foodservice Finance manages PepsiCo’s on-premise business, which is comprised of full-service vending, national accounts (Subway, Buffalo Wild Wings, etc.) and regional accounts. Foodservice Finance encompasses many functions including FP&A, sales finance and capital planning. Supply Chain Finance manages the company’s product manufacturing and distribution strategies by analyzing production, labor, transportation and selling costs. Supply Chain associates assess the historical and projected financial economics of producing and selling company products. Associates also evaluate productivity initiatives and perform capacity analyses to drive critical capital decisions and inform production planning. Business Transformation Finance provides strategic financial direction against transformative programs and workstreams set to influence the way that PepsiCo operates in the short and long term. Business Transformation Finance touches all the other functional areas listed as well. What you can expect: While we will provide you with an initial onboarding training and ongoing function specific development, we also encourage you to develop yourself through our vast learning labs. Keep in mind, when you work for PepsiCo, you will have access to a variety of operating models within the Beverage, Foods and Corporate environments; this means that you can support power brands such as Gatorade, Quaker & Frito-Lay and still work within the same company! jobs.title: FP&A Analyst - Digital Planning
jobs.description: Overview We Are PepsiCo Join PepsiCo and Dare for Better! We are the perfect place for curious people, thinkers and change agents. From leadership to front lines, we're excited about the future and working together to make the world a better place. Being part of PepsiCo means being part of one of the largest food and beverage companies in the world, with our iconic brands consumed more than a billion times a day in more than 200 countries. Our product portfolio, which includes 22 of the world's most iconic brands, such as Sabritas, Gamesa, Quaker, Pepsi, Gatorade and Sonrics, has been a part of Mexican homes for more than 116 years. A career at PepsiCo means working in a culture where all people are welcome. Here, you can dare to be you. No matter who you are, where you're from, or who you love, you can always influence the people around you and make a positive impact in the world. Know more: PepsiCoJobs Join PepsiCo, dare for better. Responsibilities The Opportunity At PepsiCo, we are transforming the way we plan, analyze, and make business decisions by combining Finance expertise with digital capabilities and advanced planning technologies. As part of PepsiCo’s global Plan capability, IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) is a key enabler of this transformation. The platform provides an integrated and predictive planning environment that helps Finance teams streamline planning processes, improve data connectivity, and enable more agile decision-making. IBM Planning Analytics is currently deployed across multiple PepsiCo sectors and continues to expand globally. As part of the Global Digital Planning team, you will support the continued evolution of the solution across PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA), PepsiCo Foods North America (PFNA) and LATAM Foods. This role sits at the intersection of Finance, Technology, and the Business. You will work closely with Finance and cross-functional stakeholders to understand business needs, translate them into practical solutions, and continuously improve the way planning processes are executed. A Facility Operations Manager (FOM) plays a vital role in the Frito-Lay supply chain, driving results and managing change related to all operations functions at a Distribution Center site. Specifically, a FOM at Frito-Lay has three overarching responsibilities: people and team development, site management, and customer service. Direct expenses include labor efficiency (how many cases are outputted per hour worked) and accuracy (packing cases in a complete and exact manner). A heavy emphasis will be placed on supporting the frontline Team to achieve its Dynamic Standards Labor expectations. Additionally, all indirect expenses must be maintained, such as supplies, utilities, etc Ensure site regulatory compliance with OSHA, DOT, FDA, and EPA Manage warehouse space from both inventory and safety standpoints. jobs.title: Strategy Sr Manager – Technology & Digital Transformation
jobs.description: Overview The Strategy Sr Manager – Technology & Digital Transformation works closely with the Head of Technology Strategy to drive PepsiCo’s Technology vision and Strategy. This role involves identifying and analyzing emerging technology trends, conducting industry outreach, benchmarking, identifying key strategic decisions, and providing thought leadership. The Senior Manager will develop both immediate and long-term technology visions, formulate strategic decisions, and create a comprehensive global tech strategy framework that aligns with business priorities. They will analyze technology spend, benchmark against industry standards, and recommend investment areas to maintain a competitive edge. A significant aspect of this role involves defining PepsiCo’s technology investment strategy. This includes assisting the Board of Directors (BOD) and PepsiCo Executive Committee (PEC) in prioritizing and reallocating spending across the business, guided by our internal enterprise strategy and the evolving technology landscape. In an era of record investments in technology to maintain a competitive edge and rapid advancements in tech adoption (e.g., GenAI, quantum computing, computer vision), intentionality is crucial for PepsiCo’s success. This role is vital in understanding and anticipating trends, setting PepsiCo’s technology vision, and recommending substantial changes to our tech investments. It requires not only grasping the trends but also aligning new technologies with sources of competitive advantage. As our peers become increasingly aggressive with their tech strategies, PepsiCo needs the insight and vision to stay ahead. Additionally, the role includes developing a technology roadmap, defining success markers, and ensuring adaptability to evolving needs. Expertise in 2-3 key technology areas such as Infrastructure, Architecture, or Product Management is critical. The Senior manager will engage with senior stakeholders, communicate complex concepts clearly, and build strong relationships to support technology initiatives. They will also participate in industry forums, gather insights, and represent the organization externally. Conceptual problem-solving and storytelling skills are crucial for addressing challenges and inspiring stakeholders. This position offers the opportunity to shape the future of our enterprise technology and make a significant impact. Responsibilities Mega Trends and Perspectives Identify and Analyze Emerging Technology Trends: Focus on the evolving aspects of people, processes, and technology. This includes understanding shifts in business processes due to digital transformation, and the adoption of cutting-edge technologies like AI. Conduct Industry Outreach: Engage with industry experts and peers through conferences, webinars, and direct communication. Gather insights on the latest trends and strategic moves by peers to benchmark and identify best practices. Provide Thought Leadership: Develop detailed reports and presentations on mega trends, offering strategic recommendations. Highlight how these trends can impact the organization and suggest ways to leverage them for competitive advantage. Create and Maintain an Ongoing List of Inspiring Case Examples: Compile and regularly update a list of successful technology implementations and innovations. Use these case studies to inform and inspire PepsiCo's technology strategy, ensuring it stays current with industry best practices. Technology vision and strategy Develop and Articulate the Immediate, Medium-Term, and Long-Term Technology Vision: Create a comprehensive technology vision that aligns with industry trends, business priorities, and PepsiCo's current maturity. This vision should outline a clear path for technological growth and innovation. Formulate Big Bet Decisions: Identify and prioritize major strategic initiatives that will shape the enterprise technology strategy. These "big bets" should focus on transformative projects and investments that have the potential to significantly impact PepsiCo's future success. Connect the Dots Between Existing Capabilities: Analyze and integrate current technological capabilities to form a cohesive Global Tech Strategy. This involves identifying synergies and gaps, ensuring that all technology efforts are aligned and contribute to the overall strategic objectives. Ensure Business Priorities Inform Technology Strategy: Establish a dynamic feedback loop where business priorities continuously shape the technology strategy, and vice versa. This ensures that technological initiatives are always aligned with business goals, fostering a collaborative environment where technology and business strategies mutually reinforce each other Technology Spend and External Benchmarking Analyze Our S&T Spend and Compare It Against Industry Benchmarks: Conduct a thorough analysis of the PepsiCo S&T spend. Compare these figures with industry benchmarks to identify areas where PepsiCo is over or under-investing. Identify Directional Targets, Areas of Investment, and Key Focus Areas: Based on the analysis, pinpoint specific targets and areas where investment is needed to maintain or enhance PepsiCo's competitive edge. This includes identifying emerging technologies, strategic initiatives, and key focus areas that align with PepsiCo's long-term goals. Provide Recommendations on Optimizing Technology Spend: Offer strategic recommendations to optimize technology spending. This involves suggesting ways to reallocate resources, reduce inefficiencies, and invest in high-impact areas. The goal is to ensure that technology investments are aligned with strategic objectives and deliver maximum value to PepsiC Technology Roadmap Develop a Consolidated Technology Roadmap: Create a comprehensive technology roadmap that aligns with PepsiCo's vision and business priorities. This roadmap should integrate various technological initiatives and projects, providing a clear path forward that supports strategic goals and ensures cohesive progress across PepsiCo. Define Key Markers of Success (OKRs/KPIs): Establish clear Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the success of initiatives outlined in the roadmap. These markers will help track progress, identify areas for improvement, and ensure that all efforts are aligned with the overall strategic objectives. Ensure the Roadmap is Adaptable: Design the roadmap to be flexible and adaptable to evolving business needs and technological advancements. This involves regularly reviewing and updating the roadmap to reflect changes in the business environment, emerging technologies, and shifting priorities, ensuring that PepsiCo remains agile and responsive to new opportunities and challenges. Compensation and Benefits: The expected compensation range for this position is between $123,500 - $206,750. Location, confirmed job-related skills, experience, and education will be considered in setting actual starting salary. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range during the hiring process. Bonus based on performance and eligibility target payout is 15% of annual salary paid out annually. Paid time off subject to eligibility, including paid parental leave, vacation, sick, and bereavement. In addition to salary, PepsiCo offers a comprehensive benefits package to support our employees and their families, subject to elections and eligibility: Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Health, and Dependent Care Reimbursement Accounts, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Insurance (Accident, Group Legal, Life), Defined Contribution Retirement Plan. Qualifications Conceptual Problem Solving: Proficiency in addressing complex technology challenges through innovative problem-solving techniques. Leadership and Influence: Ability to inspire and engage stakeholders at all levels, driving collaboration and support for technology initiatives Storytelling and Communication: Exceptional storytelling skills to communicate complex concepts clearly and compellingly to diverse audiences. Industry Outreach and Networking: Experience in participating in industry forums, gathering insights, and representing PepsiCo externally. Technology Roadmap Development: Expertise in creating and managing a comprehensive technology roadmap that aligns with strategic goals. Relationship Building: Strong interpersonal skills to build and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Adaptability: Ability to adapt strategies and plans to evolving business needs and technological advancements. Expertise in Key Technology Areas: Deep knowledge in 2-3 key technology areas such as Infrastructure, Architecture, or Product Management. Experience 8 - 12 years’ work experience with either internal or external strategy experience (top-tier consulting firm experience preferred) Multi-functional experience, working with support functions (e.g., IT, Finance) and business EEO Statement Our Company will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, and all other applicable laws, including but not limited to, San Francisco Police Code Sections 4901-4919, commonly referred to as the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance; and Chapter XVII, Article 9 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code, commonly referred to as the Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance. jobs.title: Supply Chain Capability & Innovation Senior Manager
jobs.description: Overview The Senior Manager, Supply Chain Capability & Innovation Senior Manager is accountable for defining and leading the strategic capability agenda for PGCS Supply Chain. The role exists to simplify, standardise and automate end-to-end Supply Chain processes, strengthen Supply Chain Master Data Governance, and ensure that analytics, digital and process investments are aligned to business priorities and measurable value creation. The role acts as the primary Supply Chain business interface with central PGCS D&AI, leading portfolio scoping, solution design input, prioritisation, agile delivery support, business testing and adoption. The role also leads Demand Planning best practice implementation across PGCS International Hubs, with a primary focus on Ireland and Singapore. Responsibilities Supply Chain Capability Strategy and Transformation Leadership Define and lead the Supply Chain Capability, Innovation and Process Excellence roadmap for PGCS. Identify strategic opportunities to simplify, standardise and automate end-to-end Supply Chain processes. Translate business priorities into practical capability programmes that improve service, inventory, productivity and planning effectiveness. Lead cross-functional transformation initiatives across Supply Chain, Operations, Finance, Technology and D&AI. Act as a senior advisor to Supply Chain leadership on process maturity, digital enablement and capability development. Master Data Governance Leadership Own the Supply Chain Master Data Governance agenda, including governance model, stewardship approach, process controls and accountability framework. Improve quality, ownership and usability of Supply Chain master data across material, BOM, vendor, planning and related data domains. Partner with central data, technology and functional stakeholders to align MDG priorities with enterprise data and transformation objectives. Establish routines, standards and performance measures that sustain master data quality and governance maturity. Represent Supply Chain requirements in relevant data governance, technology and process forums. Supply Chain Analytics Portfolio Support the alignment of SC analytics and ways of working with global D&AI operating model. Support agile delivery through backlog input, sprint engagement, business testing, acceptance criteria and issue resolution. Ensure analytics and digital products are deployed effectively, adopted by users and measured against business value outcomes. End-to-End Process Simplification, Standardisation and Automation Lead the redesign of Supply Chain processes to remove complexity, reduce manual effort and improve reliability. Establish common process standards and best practices across relevant international Supply Chain operations. Identify opportunities for automation, workflow enablement, advanced analytics and AI-supported decision making. Partner with functional and technology teams to embed controls, standard work and sustainable process ownership. Drive continuous improvement in planning, inventory, master data, customer collaboration and operational decision processes. Demand Planning Best Practice Deployment Define and lead the Demand Planning capability improvement agenda across PGCS International Hubs, with primary focus on Ireland and Singapore. Deploy best practice forecasting, demand review, governance and performance management processes. Partner with Commercial, Finance, Supply Chain, Operations and D&AI teams to improve demand signal quality and planning discipline. Support the development and adoption of analytics-enabled forecasting and demand planning decision support. Drive continuous improvement in forecast accuracy, bias management, planning stability and cross-functional demand alignment. Change Leadership and Capability Building Lead adoption of new processes, tools, analytics solutions and digital ways of working across Supply Chain teams. Build organisational capability through training, coaching, playbooks, governance routines and structured change plans. Develop approaches that accelerate knowledge capture and reduce reliance on fragmented or individual SME knowledge. Champion data-driven decision making, standard work and continuous improvement across the PGCS Supply Chain community. Ensure capability changes are embedded sustainably with clear ownership, adoption metrics and leadership sponsorship. Senior Stakeholder and Matrix Leadership Influence senior stakeholders across Supply Chain, D&AI, Technology, Finance, Operations and international hub leadership. Align diverse stakeholder groups around shared priorities, resourcing choices and transformation outcomes. Balance global standardisation with practical hub-level adoption requirements. Represent Supply Chain needs in enterprise transformation and technology discussions. Lead through influence in a complex, matrixed and international environment. Qualifications Education Bachelor degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Information Systems, Data, Analytics or related discipline. Master degree, professional Supply Chain qualification, Lean Six Sigma, APICS, IBP, data governance or product management certification preferred. Experience 10 or more years of progressive experience in Supply Chain, transformation, capability development, analytics, process excellence, master data governance or digital enablement. Demonstrated success leading complex cross-functional transformation agendas within a global or matrixed organisation. Strong understanding of demand planning, supply planning, inventory management, master data, SAP-enabled planning processes and end-to-end supply chain operations. Experience partnering with Data & Analytics, Technology or Product teams to scope, design, test, deploy and adopt analytics or digital solutions. Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, shape strategic roadmaps and deliver measurable business value through process and capability change. Experience implementing planning best practices across multiple sites, hubs or geographies preferred.

Comfortable with and effective communicating (verbal and written) with all stakeholders, across global markets. Treats all people with respect and fairness; open is to and respectful of others’ opinions and points of view Takes initiative to find ways to get better results, seeks and takes advantage of ideas, best practices and solutions.

Responsibilities Partner with commercial lead team to develop a robust business Revenue strategy to accelerate NRR growth. Develop detailed AOP Pricing plan to be executed – outlining key RM initiatives, timing, and financial impacts Drive the creation of market portfolio pricing strategy, development of annual pricing plans/recommended actions and overall management of the local market pricing practice. Develop robust Pack Price architecture based on insights and data analysis. Ensure full accomplishment of Pack Price strategy across all channels while aligning Commercial/Category Team on optimal use of different pricing levers. jobs.title: People Operations Asst Analyst
jobs.description: Overview People Experience & Operations Asst Analyst is the on-site HR SPOC for employees. Typically, responsible for managing the day-to-day operations, acting as a first-tier support for all HR related matters on site. Starting from onboarding coordination and throughout the employment duration. The role is the one face to governmental bodies inspectors and hence is accountable to keep and maintain complete/accurate and up to date documents on-site. Being part of the Global People Experience & Operations Team, this role is expected to provide consistent and standard services and achieve high level of employee satisfaction through systems training, process orientation and SLA adherence as measured by global reporting tools. The role is also expected to activate launches and change management tactics of new digital tools and solutions (ex: iCIMS, ServiceNow). Responsibilities Onboarding & New Hire Integration Manage hiring documentation, including physical receipt and collection of required wet signatures. Coordinate end-to-end onboarding experience, including site walkthrough and facilitation of business tools/assets handover from relevant departments. Follow up with Hiring Managers to ensure completion of onboarding tasks. Train new hires on PEP tools and systems to enable smooth integration. Systems, Tools & Digital Adoption Drive effective utilization of HR systems and tools by: Training employees on platforms such as MyServices, iCIMS, MS Teams, Smiles, etc. Monitoring systems adoption and partnering with stakeholders to improve usage. Compliance, Employee Relations & Governance Ensure compliance with internal policies and local regulations by: Maintaining legally required documentation and up-to-date health certificates. Running periodic audits aligned with government and legal requirements. Supporting site government inspections, handling queries, and reporting outcomes to the legal & ER teams. Communicating ER, Compliance & Ethics, and Legal outcomes from internal investigations to employees and ensuring proper acknowledgment (wet signature and system capture). Supporting communication cascade through available channels and encouraging activities participation. Offboarding & Employee Exit Management Ensure smooth employee exit processes by tracking and following up on clearance activities through myServices and other relevant systems. Coordinate with stakeholders to ensure timely completion of exit requirements and approvals. Maintain proper documentation and employee acknowledgements in line with compliance and legal requirements. Learning & Development Support the learning agenda by: Managing logistics for training sessions (venue booking, meeting room readiness, catering). Delivering, tracking, and following up on compliance, ethics, and TM-related face-to-face training sessions. Monitoring trainings participation and completion rates. Qualifications 1–3 years of experience, preferably with HR Operations experience. Customer Orientation. Technical / Functional Skills & Knowledge of HR Tools and Interfaces. Experience or understanding of HR Operations / Shared Services environment. Change management and agility. Must possess strong influencing skills. Demonstrated track record of strong service delivery.

jobs.title: Co-Man Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description: Overview Work for a global FMCG company with some of the world’s most trusted and iconic brands. Be part of an exciting business where employees are recognized and career growth is supported.  At PepsiCo, you can Dare for Better. You can help build a world where there are more possibilities for more people, no matter what role you hold. Together, we’ll make a positive impact for good. Because when we Dare for Better, we can smile at what’s next. For our careers, families, communities and the planet. The Co-Manufacturing Supply Chain Manager will lead end-to-end Supply Chain management for Quaker co-manufacturing operations across Malaysia and the Philippines (total 4 co-mans), ensuring supply continuity, 98%+ service level, and effective co-man performance across 10 markets. The role provides overall governance of co-man operations, including capacity and materials planning, forecast alignment, inventory control, NPI/label transitions, service performance, and issue resolution. The role also leads regional oats supply strategy and planning across Quaker co-mans, including management of multiple oats sources, while driving continuous improvement, cost and process optimization, and strong cross-functional collaboration with Commercial, Procurement, PD, Quality and Project teams. Additionally, the role will also provide Supply Chain support for any new co-manufacturing operations established outside Malaysia and the Philippines, including setup, onboarding and integration into the regional supply network Responsibilities What you will be responsible for: 1. Co-Man Operations & Supply Planning Lead end-to-end supply chain operations for Quaker co-manufacturers across Malaysia and the Philippines, ensuring 98%+ service level and reliable supply to all markets. Manage order fulfilment, production planning, capacity, shipment execution and forecast accuracy across multiple co-manufacturing sites. Lead regular operational reviews with co-manufacturers to monitor performance, resolve issues and drive timely corrective actions. Review market forecasts and identify supply risks, constraints and opportunities, including contingency plans where required. Manage co-man capacity against demand (C2D) and provide early escalation of potential supply risks. Coordinate raw material and packaging material planning with co-mans, suppliers and market units to maintain healthy inventory buffers and uninterrupted production. Establish and maintain effective ways of working and governance with new and existing co-manufacturers. Ensure co-man service level scorecards, inventory reports and operational data are maintained accurately and submitted on time. 2. Co-Man Performance & Continuous Improvement Drive continuous improvement initiatives with co-manufacturers to improve service, lead time, capacity flexibility and operational efficiency. Identify and implement productivity and process improvement opportunities across the co-man network. Partner with Procurement, R&D, Marketing, GP and other functional teams on supplier qualification, product trials and productivity initiatives. Ensure reliable supplier performance and lead resolution of operational issues and commercial disputes. Support supply network optimization, capacity expansion and lead-time reduction initiatives. 3. Oats Supply Strategy & Capacity Planning Lead monthly oats supply strategy and allocation planning across Quaker co-manufacturers. Consolidate oats demand and consumption requirements and develop appropriate inventory buffer strategies to mitigate supply risks. Secure supply confirmation with GP and Quaker oats plant and develop alternative sourcing strategies where supply gaps are identified. Manage short- and long-term co-man capacity planning for multiple co-man sites, aligned with demand and business growth. Support development of regional supply network strategies to improve supply resilience and flexibility. 4. New Product Introduction & Project Management Lead Supply Chain activities for new product introduction, innovation and product / artwork transition projects across Asia Foods markets. Partner with regional cross-functional teams to ensure production readiness, material availability and seamless integration of new products into the replenishment process. Lead artwork and packaging transitions, including material run-down planning, to meet project timelines and minimize material write-off. Coordinate with co-mans, suppliers, customers and logistics partners to ensure timely and cost-effective shipment execution. Negotiate and align with co-manufacturers and suppliers on minimum run quantities, lead times and operational requirements. Support Business Continuity Planning (BCP) initiatives across the co-man network. 5. SNOE/SNOP, Forecast and Order Management Lead the SNOE/SNOP agenda for the co-man portfolio, consolidating demand and supply inputs, highlighting key risks and constraints, and driving alignment on replenishment and supply actions. Consolidate and process market orders, monitor order fulfilment and ensure production and shipment timelines are achieved. Drive forecast accuracy tracking and proactively identify forecast and supply risks. Ensure co-manufacturers execute production according to market-requested timelines and support timely month-end closing. Maintain accurate service level, inventory, capacity and operational performance reporting. Provide data and analysis to Sector and Global teams as required. Provide guidance to Supply Chain Assistants on order tracking, shipment coordination and day-to-day co-man operations. Qualifications What you will need to have: Minimum 7-8 years of relevant experience in Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Logistics, Demand/Supply Planning or related functions, preferably with co-manufacturing / FMCG experience. Proven experience in co-manufacturer / supplier management, including performance management, capacity planning, service level management and issue resolution. Strong experience in SNOE/SNOP, demand & supply planning, order management and forecast alignment. Experience in managing New Product Introduction (NPI), product transitions, line trials and commercialization projects. Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret data, identify supply risks and translate insights into actionable plans. Strong problem-solving and logical thinking skills, with a proactive approach to identifying and resolving supply issues. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across Commercial, Manufacturing, Procurement, R&D, Quality and regional teams. Strong project management skills, with the ability to lead multiple priorities and deliver projects within agreed timelines. Good understanding of capacity planning, inventory management, supply risk mitigation and Business Continuity Planning (BCP). Working knowledge of trade agreements, tariff structures and cross-border supply / import-export processes is an advantage. Proficient in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word; strong data analysis and reporting capability. Highly organized, detail-oriented and able to work independently in a complex, multi-market environment. Ability to work effectively across different cultures and geographies.

jobs.title: Business Development Manager, Global Portable Snacking
jobs.description: Overview CAREERS TO SMILE ABOUT At PepsiCo, you’ll discover a place where our mission is to create smiles around the world. With a portfolio of more than 500 beloved brands including, Gatorade, Lay’s and Quaker, our work touches millions of people every day. At the heart of the company is a team of thinkers, creators, and problem-solvers who collaborate to innovate and turn ideas into action. Driven by innovation and a focus on creating joyful moments through food and drinks, our decisions are guided by consumer centricity, creating opportunities for our associates to do meaningful work and make a lasting impact in the communities we serve. Whatever your role, you’ll be part of a global community that values your ideas and empowers you to make an impact, on your career and on the world around you. Responsibilities Business Development Manager, Global Portable Snacking The Opportunity in Plano, Texas PepsiCo is building the next wave of growth in portable snacking, bringing together global brands, advantaged formats, and new ways to reach consumers across markets and channels. As part of PepsiCo’s Global Imports & Portable Snacking business, you’ll help shape and scale a high-priority growth platform with an ambition to reach $3–4B in business by 2030, while building a sustainable, high-margin model across markets. In this role, you’ll connect strategy with execution—identifying where the biggest opportunities exist, shaping market and portfolio priorities, and working with teams across the business to turn those opportunities into actionable plans. You’ll partner closely with Strategy, Marketing, Commercial, Supply Chain, Operations, and local market teams to determine where PepsiCo should play, how we should win, and what capabilities and investments are needed to accelerate growth. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex business questions, working across functions and markets, and turning insights into decisions that have a tangible impact on a growing global business. What You’ll Do Shape the long-term opportunity: Partner with Strategy to define the growth opportunity for portable snacking, including market potential, key growth drivers, and priorities across geographies. Turn strategy into action: Translate long-term ambitions into clear priorities, decisions, and actions that can be incorporated into near-term business plans. Identify growth opportunities: Analyze market dynamics, competitive trends, consumer insights, and business performance to identify priority markets and whitespace opportunities. Shape the portfolio strategy: Work with Marketing and cross-functional partners to define the future role of portable snacking formats—including Stax, Minis, and Square Canisters—and how they can drive growth across different markets. Build market and investment plans: Partner with local teams to develop market-level plans, including format priorities, launch sequencing, and investment opportunities. Build fact-based business cases to help prioritize resources. Scale opportunities globally: Connect markets to identify transferable opportunities, best practices, and synergies that can accelerate growth across the portfolio. Lead strategic initiatives: Drive or support high-impact, cross-functional projects that strengthen the business model, value chain, and future growth opportunities. Influence senior stakeholders: Bring a strategic point of view to leadership discussions, highlighting opportunities, gaps, trade-offs, and areas requiring deeper analysis. Qualifications What We’re Looking For Approximately 5 years of experience in strategy, business development, management consulting, or a related strategic role; global or multi-market experience is a plus. Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure complex or ambiguous business questions and translate them into actionable recommendations. Commercial acumen and the ability to connect market opportunities, portfolio decisions, operations, and financial considerations. Experience working across functions and influencing stakeholders without direct authority. Strong analytical skills and the ability to use data, market insights, and business cases to support strategic decisions. Ability to bring an external perspective, challenge conventional thinking, and identify new approaches to growth. Strong communication and storytelling skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information for senior audiences. Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve and solutions are not always clearly defined. Why PepsiCo You’ll join a global team working on a high-priority growth platform from the ground up, with the opportunity to influence strategy across markets while staying close to execution. This role offers exposure to senior leaders and cross-functional teams across Strategy, Marketing, Commercial, Supply Chain, and Operations, while giving you the opportunity to help shape how PepsiCo builds and scales new sources of growth globally. Compensation & Benefits The expected salary range for this position is USD $125,363–$155,185. Actual starting salary will be determined based on location, job-related skills, experience, education, and other relevant factors. Eligible employees may receive an annual performance-based bonus with a 12% target payout. PepsiCo offers a comprehensive benefits package, subject to eligibility and elections, including medical, dental, vision, disability coverage, health and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee assistance programs, insurance benefits, paid time off, paid parental leave, and a defined contribution retirement plan. Compensation and benefits may vary based on the employee’s work location and applicable U.S. regional guidelines. Location: Texas, United States
